answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing jobs that consume scarce timber, with each account locked to one bonded anchor. A new identity must post its own collateral and wait through a spiral of randomized audits; copied profiles cannot reuse another account’s bond or work history. If an audit finds duplicate control, the bond is slashed and the agent loses accrued weight. Sybils therefore cost repeated capital, time, and exposure to forfeiture.
